reuse.why: Adds a new worstCaseAmount instead of changing the existing exported getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts, which already decides the missing/number/range cases and serves the desktop client.

duplication.why: The range arithmetic is now shared by the four server sites, but each keeps its own `missing ? 0 : number ? value : range` dispatch, and worstCaseAmount runs parallel to getScheduledAmount's range branch.

placement.why: A schedule-amount rule is placed in shared/rules.ts (rule condition helpers) rather than shared/schedules.ts, where the tree keeps getScheduledAmount and other schedule logic.

scope.why: Only the amount sites, the helper, its tests and a release note.

maintainability.why: Two definitions of the expected amount now disagree: getScheduledAmount (desktop balance and schedule tables) and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions still use the midpoint while the server sites use worstCaseAmount.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts, forecast-schedules.ts and schedule-template.ts call a new worstCaseAmount instead of shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount; computeSchedulePreviewTransactions in shared/schedules.ts and getScheduledAmount itself were left on the midpoint.

disguised_duplication.where: worstCaseAmount is an openly separate helper beside getScheduledAmount, not a reshaped copy.

one_place.where: The rule lands in worstCaseAmount (shared/rules.ts) for four server sites, but getScheduledAmount and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions in shared/schedules.ts still compute the midpoint, and each site keeps its own missing/number dispatch.
